events.title: R first publicly announced
events.summary: Ross Ihaka and Robert Gentleman posted R to StatLib and announced it on the s-news mailing list in August 1993.
events.about: R is the open-source environment for statistics and data visualization — data frames, linear models, ggplot2 charts, and CRAN's package ecosystem. Data scientists, epidemiologists, and quant researchers use it for exploratory analysis, publishing reproducible research, and building Shiny web apps.

narrative.whyChosen: R became the lingua franca of academic and open statistical computing, rivaling commercial S-PLUS.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved a free, extensible stats language could outgrow its university origins and power industry data science.
narrative.problemSolved: Statisticians needed affordable, programmable software for teaching and research — commercial packages were expensive.

events.title: Apple Newton MessagePad released
events.summary: Apple began selling the Newton MessagePad in August 1993 — a PDA with handwriting recognition and an ARM610 processor.
events.about: The Newton was Apple's first ARM-based product — the ARM6 core in the MessagePad predated the Archimedes' success in phones and Macs by decades. Developers wrote NewtonScript apps; the handwriting [UI] inspired ridicule and admiration. Though commercially mixed, it proved Apple would bet on ARM and mobile form factors long before the iPhone.

narrative.whyChosen: The Newton was Apple's first PDA and among the first products using ARM processors.
narrative.whyImportant: It connected Apple's mobile ambitions to the [ARM architecture] that powers iPhones and M-series Macs today.
narrative.problemSolved: Mobile professionals needed a pocket computer for notes, contacts, and scheduling beyond paper planners.
